chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Najih, from Abul Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no problem for the one in Ihram to wear the ring.
And in another report, (He said): He should not wear it for adornment.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a pilgrim in Ihram to wear a ring?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the permissibility of wearing a ring during Ihram, distinguishing between general wear and excessive adornment. In Shia jurisprudence, this highlights the principle that minor accessories are not prohibited unless they constitute 'zina' (adornment) that distracts from the spiritual state of consecration. The distinction underscores the balance between practical utility and the humility required in the state of Ihram.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Nasr, from Najeeh, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘There is no problem for the one in Ihraam to wear the ring’.
And in another report, (He<sup>asws</sup> said): ‘He should not wear it for the adornment’.
